questions.text:
Consider a sequential digital circuit consisting of T flip-flops and D flip-flops as shown in the figure. CLKIN is the clock input to the circuit. At the beginning, Q1, Q2 and Q3 have values 0, 1 and 1, respectively.

Which one of the given values of (Q1, Q2, Q3) can NEVER be obtained with this digital circuit?
questions.solution:
From the circuit: [latex]T_1=\overline{Q_3}[/latex], [latex]D_2=Q_1[/latex], [latex]T_3=Q_2[/latex].
Next state: [latex]Q_1^+=Q_1\oplus\overline{Q_3}[/latex], [latex]Q_2^+=Q_1[/latex], [latex]Q_3^+=Q_3\oplus Q_2[/latex].

Starting from (0, 1, 1):
011 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 000 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 100 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 010 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 110 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 011 (repeats)

(0, 0, 1) never appears.

Answer: (0, 0, 1)

questions.text:
A particular number is written as 132 in radix-4 representation. The same number
in radix-5 representation is _____.
questions.solution:
[latex](132)_4=1\times16+3\times4+2=30[/latex]

Convert 30 to base 5: [latex]30=1\times25+1\times5+0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex](110)_5[/latex]

Answer: 110

questions.text:
The output of a 2-input multiplexer is connected back to one of its inputs as shown in the figure.

Match the functional equivalence of this circuit to one of the following options.
questions.solution:
The output Q is fed back to input 0.
- S = 1: Q follows input 1 (the data input D).
- S = 0: Q = Q, so it holds its old value.

It is transparent while S = 1 and holds while S = 0, which is a level-triggered D latch (S acts as enable). There is no clock edge, so it is not a flip-flop.

Answer: D Latch

questions.text:
Consider three floating point numbers A, B and C stored in registers [latex]R_A[/latex], [latex]R_B[/latex] and [latex]R_C[/latex], respectively as per IEEE-754 single precision floating point format. The 32-bit content stored in these registers (in hexadecimal form) are as follows.

[latex]R_A=0xC1400000[/latex]
[latex]R_B=0x42100000[/latex]
[latex]R_C=0x41400000[/latex]

Which one of the following is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Decode each number (sign | exponent | mantissa):
- [latex]R_A=[/latex] C1400000: sign 1, exponent [latex]130\Rightarrow2^3[/latex], mantissa 1.1[latex]{}_2[/latex] = 1.5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]A=-12[/latex]
- [latex]R_B=[/latex] 42100000: sign 0, exponent [latex]132\Rightarrow2^5[/latex], mantissa 1.001[latex]{}_2[/latex] = 1.125 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]B=36[/latex]
- [latex]R_C=[/latex] 41400000: same as A but positive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]C=12[/latex]

- [latex]A+C=0[/latex] True
- [latex]A+B=24\ne12=C[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] FALSE
- [latex]B=36=3C[/latex] True
- [latex]B-C=24 \gt 0[/latex] True

Answer: C = A + B

questions.text: Let R1 and R2 be two 4-bit registers that store numbers in 2's complement form. For the operation R1+R2, which one of the following values of R1 and R2 gives an arithmetic overflow?
questions.solution:
4-bit 2's complement range: [latex]-8[/latex] to [latex]+7[/latex].

- 1011 + 1110 = [latex](-5)+(-2)=-7[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits
- 1100 + 1010 = [latex](-4)+(-6)=-10[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] overflow
- 0011 + 0100 = [latex]3+4=7[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits
- 1001 + 1111 = [latex](-7)+(-1)=-8[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits

Answer: R1 = 1100 and R2 = 1010
